findings.explanation: The save dialog selects the results filename, but exporting results.csv also truncates an existing results_TACs.csv without asking about that separate file. A user can lose unrelated existing data even when the selected results filename was new.

items.title: Fit all excludes a segment even when the input is a plasma file

findings.title: Fit all excludes a segment even when the input is a plasma file
findings.evidence:
def fitSegments(self, analysis, modelKey, referenceId=None, options=None, plasma=None, segmentIds=None,
                    progress=None):
        """{segment ID: result} of every segment (but the reference) or of segmentIds; a segment that cannot be
        fitted gets {"error": text}."""
        inputFunction, reference, blood = self.inputs(analysis, modelKey, referenceId, plasma)
        ids = [s for s in (segmentIds or analysis.segments) if s != referenceId]
findings.explanation: The GUI always selects a reference segment, including for plasma-file models; this unconditional exclusion skips that segment in Fit all. With one target segment and a plasma curve, preview is allowed but Fit all produces no segment result.
findings.suggestion: Allow an optional whole-blood segment for plasma-file models and include the selected target in batch fitting when it is not actually being used as a reference input.

items.title: Missing target-frame values are treated as zero in SUVR

findings.title: Missing target-frame values are treated as zero in SUVR
findings.evidence:
target = float(np.nansum(w * tissue) / w.sum())
    ref = float(np.nansum(w * reference.frameMeans()) / w.sum())
    suvr = _ratio(target, ref)
findings.explanation: When a target segment has no voxels on some frame grids, segmentCurves records NaN for those frames, but this sum ignores the missing numerator while retaining its duration in the denominator. If the reference is present and the target exists in at least one frame, SUVR can be reported too low without a missing-data warning.
findings.suggestion: Reject incomplete curves or compute both target and reference on a common set of finite frames, with an explicit warning.

items.title: Prepending module directory to sys.path at module import

findings.title: Prepending module directory to sys.path at module import
findings.explanation: Each scripted module (`DICOMGatedDynamicPET.py`, `DynamicPETEditor.py`, `DynamicPETModeling.py`, `DynamicPETMotionCorrection.py`, `DynamicPETRegistration.py`, `GatedDynamicPETSettings.py`) inserts its module directory at the front of `sys.path` if not already present. Slicer already adds scripted module directories to `sys.path` or supports importing helper packages placed alongside the module script, and the modules/packages here use distinct names (`DICOMGatedDynamicPETLib`, `DynamicPET*`), so the risk of name collisions with standard or bundled libraries is very low.
findings.suggestion: Rely on Slicer's standard module path handling or append rather than prepend to `sys.path` if needed for standalone testing.

The UI's cancellation callback returns `not dialog.wasCanceled` (1635-1640), but lines 1645-1646 cache the resulting analysis, so canceling can leave incomplete data treated as complete rather than discard it. Fit-all also returns partial results on cancellation (342-344). There are positive features: map work has progress and cancellation (1911-1928), cleanup removes observers (2009-2012), and Testing/test_kinetics.py:1-4 describes independent simulated-curve tests. These were inspected, not run.
